_meta.purpose: Two playbooks: (1) candidate challenges while preparing; (2) working-professional situations. Each is a diagnose → act → escalate checklist.
_meta.disclaimer: Workplace guides are educational frameworks, not legal, tax or audit advice. For a live engagement, confirm against current standards and consult your firm's technical/quality team or a qualified advisor.

challenges.title: I work full-time and can't find study hours
symptoms: Forgetting what you studied last week
actions: Plan 75–90 minutes on weekdays (e.g., 45 minutes before work + 30 minutes of questions at lunch) instead of weekend marathons.
Use this app's Daily Review on your commute. It only shows the questions due today.
Book your exam date first. A fixed deadline beats an open-ended plan.
Block one 'catch-up' slot per week for days that go wrong.
challenges.metric: At least 5 study days a week, and Daily Review cleared at least 80% of days.

challenges.title: I'm scared of maths and formulas
actions: Start every formula with its story (see the Learn tab), then the formula.
Write each formula once a day for a week. Spaced recall beats re-reading.
Do the same 5 calculation types until you get 5 right in a row before moving on.
Learn your exam's calculator (financial calculator for FRM/CMA-US; check permitted models for ICAI/ICMAI).
challenges.metric: Calculation accuracy above 70% in the Progress tab.

challenges.title: I understand topics but forget them by exam day
symptoms: High score when learning, low score in mocks
actions: Stop re-reading. Test yourself instead. Retrieval practice is the most reliable memory technique.
Trust the spaced-repetition schedule: questions return after 1, 3, 7, 14 and 30 days.
Spend the final 3 weeks on mixed mocks only, no new topics.
challenges.metric: Weak-topic list shrinking week over week.

challenges.title: I freeze or run out of time in the exam
actions: Set a per-question budget (roughly the exam time divided by the number of questions) and practise with the Mock timer.
Two-pass rule: answer the sure ones first, flag the rest, and come back.
Never leave an MCQ blank unless there is negative marking. Check your exam's rules; for example, some ICAI MCQ papers and FRM/CPA scoring differ.
Breathing reset: 4 seconds in, 6 seconds out, three times, when you feel the freeze.
challenges.metric: Mocks finished with at least 5 minutes to spare.

challenges.title: I failed a section. What now?
actions: Use the score report's weak-area ranking. Re-study only the 'weaker' areas first.
Check exam-specific rules: e.g., CPA credit windows, and ICAI exemption/set-off rules for individual papers.
Reschedule within about 8–10 weeks while the material is still fresh.
Run this app's Mock filtered to your weak papers twice a week.
challenges.metric: Two consecutive mocks at 75% or above before the retake.

challenges.title: English is not my first language
actions: Circle trigger words: NOT, EXCEPT, MOST, LEAST, FIRST.
Read the LAST sentence of a long question first. It tells you what is being asked.
Build a personal glossary. Every 'trap' note in this app is a vocabulary lesson.
challenges.metric: Fewer than 1 in 10 wrong answers caused by misreading.

workplace.title: Month-end: bank reconciliation won't tie
steps: Confirm the opening balances agree to last month's signed-off reconciliation.
Match items both ways: book→bank and bank→book. Export both sides to Excel and use XLOOKUP on amount + date ±3 days.
Classify every unmatched item: timing (outstanding cheques, deposits in transit), bank-only (charges, interest, direct debits) or error.
Post journal entries only for bank-only items and errors. Timing items need no entry.
Any unexplained difference must be investigated, not 'plugged'. Escalate anything above your materiality threshold.
redFlags: The same person posting and reconciling

workplace.title: My manager asks me to delay recording an expense to hit targets
workplace.framework: AICPA Code / IMA Statement of Ethical Professional Practice / ICAI Code of Ethics: integrity, objectivity
steps: Clarify the facts: is there a genuine accounting basis (e.g., the expense really belongs to the next period)? Ask for the documentation.
If there is no basis, explain the standard (accrual principle; matching) in writing, and propose the correct treatment.
Follow your organisation's escalation path: next-level management, then the audit committee, then the ethics hotline.
Document the discussion contemporaneously.
Seek confidential advice (IMA ethics helpline, ICAI ethical guidance, or a lawyer) before any external disclosure.

workplace.title: Is there a lease hidden inside this service contract?
workplace.framework: ASC 842-10-15 / Ind AS 116 / IFRS 16: definition of a lease
steps: Is there an IDENTIFIED asset (explicitly or implicitly specified, with no substantive substitution right for the supplier)?
Does the customer get substantially all the economic benefits from using it during the period?
Does the customer direct HOW and FOR WHAT PURPOSE the asset is used?
If all three are yes, it contains a lease. Separate the lease and non-lease components (or elect the practical expedient where permitted).
Document the analysis in a technical memo for the auditors.
redFlags: Supplier can't practically swap the asset

workplace.title: Our desk breached VaR limits three days running
steps: Confirm the breach is real: check P&L (hypothetical vs actual), market data and position feeds.
Notify risk management and the desk head per the limit policy. Breaches usually need same-day escalation.
Diagnose: a new position, a volatility regime shift (model is stale), or a data error.
Agree remediation: reduce or hedge positions, or obtain a temporary limit increase approved by the right authority.
Log the exceptions for backtesting. Repeated exceptions may signal model recalibration is needed.
redFlags: Limit increased after the breach without proper approval

workplace.title: Vendor's GST doesn't appear in GSTR-2B: can we claim ITC?
workplace.framework: CGST Act 2017 s.16 (conditions for input tax credit)
steps: Check the invoice appears in GSTR-2B for the period. Credit is generally restricted to what is reflected there.
If it's missing, contact the vendor to file/correct their GSTR-1.
Hold the credit until it appears. Track it in an ITC reconciliation sheet (purchase register vs 2B).
Check the time limit for claiming ITC on that invoice under s.16(4) as currently amended.
Consider withholding vendor payment of the GST portion until compliance, as per contract terms.
